note: Scripted egocentric sessions for EgoMemo. A session is a few 30-second windows (the caption window of egomemo/run.py), each with six frames sampled every 5 seconds and written as text; the adapter turns every frame into a placeholder image and gives its text to the replaced caption model and visual encoder. No user questions are asked: the run tests the proactive service. 'ideal' says what a helpful assistant would do and is shown only to the judge; 'design' records why the session was chosen and is never sent to a model.

sessions.setting: At home in the morning: eggs on the stove, a phone call, then getting ready to leave.
sessions.design: The burner is turned on in window 1 and the user leaves the kitchen in window 2; in window 3 the camera only shows the user getting ready to leave, so a reminder about the stove needs memory. In window 4 the user goes back and turns it off, so a repeated reminder would be redundant.
sessions.ideal: Remind the user once, when they leave the kitchen or are about to leave the house (windows 2-3), that the stove is still on under the eggs. Stay silent in window 4, where the user has gone back and turned it off.
windows: Kitchen counter; my hands fill a small saucepan with water at the sink.
I place the saucepan on the front-right burner of a gas stove.
My hand turns the front-right knob; a blue flame lights under the saucepan.
I turn the knob to the highest setting; the flame is large.
I lower four eggs into the water with a spoon.
Small bubbles rise in the saucepan and steam starts to appear.
My phone on the counter lights up with an incoming call from 'Mum'.
I pick up the phone and answer it while walking out of the kitchen.
A hallway; I walk toward the living room holding the phone to my ear.
The living room; I sit down on a grey sofa.
I am still on the phone, looking out of the window.
A cushion on the sofa; my free hand plays with a tassel.
I lower the phone; the screen shows the call ended after 4 minutes.
I stand up from the sofa and walk into the hallway.
I take a black jacket from a hook by the front door.
I put on the jacket and pick up car keys from a small dish.
I sit on a bench by the door and put on my sneakers.
My hand reaches for the front door handle.
The front door is half open; I stand in the doorway.
I turn around and walk quickly back down the hallway.
In the kitchen, the saucepan is boiling hard on the front-right burner.
I turn the front-right knob off; the flame disappears.
I lift the eggs out with a spoon into a bowl.
I walk back toward the front door.

sessions.setting: Working on a laptop in a cafe, then leaving.
sessions.design: The phone is put face down on the table in window 1 and is still there in window 2; in window 3 the camera shows the user leaving without it. In window 4 the user goes back for it.
sessions.ideal: Remind the user in window 3, as they leave, that their phone is still on the table. Stay silent otherwise; in window 4 they are already going back for it.
windows: A cafe counter; I pay with my phone at the card reader.
I carry a latte to a small round table by the window.
I put my phone face down on the table next to the latte.
I take a laptop out of my backpack and open it.
The laptop screen shows a slide deck titled 'Q3 Review'.
I sip the latte.
I type notes into the slide deck.
The phone lies face down on the table beside the saucer.
I look out of the window at people passing.
I drink the rest of the latte.
I scroll through the slides on the laptop.
A waiter takes the empty cup away; the phone stays on the table.
I close the laptop and slide it into my backpack.
I stand up and put on my coat.
I sling the backpack over my shoulder and turn toward the exit.
I walk between the tables toward the glass door.
My hand pushes the glass door open.
The street outside; a bus passes.
On the pavement, I pat my coat pockets.
I turn back toward the cafe door.
Inside, I walk to the window table.
My phone lies face down on the table; I pick it up.
I put the phone in my coat pocket.
I walk out of the cafe again.

sessions.setting: Breakfast at home with a once-daily heart medication.
sessions.design: The daily tablet is taken in window 1; in window 3 the user shakes out a second tablet, which is only a mistake given window 1. In window 4 the user puts it back.
sessions.ideal: Warn the user in window 3, before they swallow it, that they already took today's tablet in window 1 (the label says one tablet daily). Stay silent otherwise.
windows: A kitchen counter with an orange pill bottle labelled 'Metoprolol 50 mg - take ONE tablet daily'.
I open the bottle and shake one white tablet into my palm.
I put the tablet in my mouth.
I drink a glass of water.
I close the bottle and put it next to the kettle.
I fill the kettle and switch it on.
I put two slices of bread into the toaster.
I take butter from the fridge.
The kettle clicks off.
I pour hot water into a mug with a tea bag.
The toast pops up; I butter it on a plate.
I eat the toast standing at the counter.
I put the plate in the sink.
I pick up the orange pill bottle next to the kettle.
I open the bottle.
I shake one white tablet into my palm.
I reach for the glass of water.
The tablet is in my palm and the glass is in my other hand.
I look at the tablet in my palm.
I put the tablet back into the bottle.
I close the bottle and put it in a cupboard.
I pick up the mug of tea.
I walk to the living room.
I sit in an armchair with the tea.

sessions.setting: Watering the garden, then a video call indoors.
sessions.design: The hose is dropped with the tap running in window 2 as the user goes indoors; in window 3 the camera only shows the call. In window 4 the user goes out and turns the tap off.
sessions.ideal: Remind the user once, in window 2 or 3, that the garden tap is still running. Do not repeat it during the call, and stay silent in window 4, where they turn it off.
windows: A garden; my hand turns on an outdoor tap on the house wall.
Water flows through a green hose.
I water a row of tomato plants with the hose.
I move along the row, watering the base of each plant.
I water a flower bed with yellow marigolds.
Puddles form on the soil.
I drop the hose on the lawn; water keeps pouring out of it.
I take my phone out of my pocket; a message reads 'Call in 2 min?'.
I walk toward the back door of the house.
I step into the kitchen and take off my garden shoes.
I walk to a desk in the study.
I sit down and open a laptop.
A video call starts on the laptop; three faces appear.
I talk, gesturing with my hand.
I take notes on a paper notepad.
I look at a shared spreadsheet on the screen.
I nod at the screen.
The call continues.
The call ends; I close the laptop.
I walk back to the kitchen.
I look out of the window; the lawn near the tomato plants is flooded.
I put on garden shoes and go outside.
I turn off the outdoor tap.
I pick up the hose and coil it.
